problems: The campfire, which is the subject, is small and hidden behind a cluster of tall upright brown planks and a grass tuft in the foreground in every frame (storyboard all 16 frames; at-25, at-50, at-75). You only see the flame through the gaps between the boards.

Caption says 'A stake beside it ends up on the ground', but no stake is seen falling. Between storyboard frames 7 and 8 a long dark stick just appears flat on the ground to the right of the fire, already at rest (at-50, at-75). Nothing tips, falls or lands.
The fallen stick is a flat, black, untextured bar that does not read as wood or as a stake (at-50, at-75).

The wind 'turning round' the fire shows only as the flame leaning one way and then another (storyboard frames 3-4 vs 8-10). Nothing else in the frame moves with the wind: the grass, the flowers and the leaves stay still. The cause is invisible.
The big yellow bird stands frozen with its arms out at the left for all 10 s (storyboard all frames). It draws the eye away from the fire and does not react to it or the wind.
It is unclear what the tall brown planks around the fire are. They look like plain boxes stuck upright in the ground and block the view rather than belong to the scene (at-25).
A pink round object lies at the foot of the fire with no clear identity (at-25, at-50).
posts.critique: The fire is boxed in behind upright planks, and the one event the caption promises, a stake ending up on the ground, happens off camera: a black bar is suddenly lying there. With the wind visible only in the flame and a frozen bird taking up the left of the frame, a viewer cannot follow what is supposed to be happening.
